intro: The AI giants are showing their cards today — Microsoft disclosed Azure and OpenAI revenue in dollars for the first time, revealing a combined $43 billion quarter that cements AI as the engine of its business, while Alphabet's $127.6 billion quarter was overshadowed by decelerating Search ad growth that sent shares tumbling 8%. Meanwhile, Google DeepMind dropped Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model laser-focused on cybersecurity that's claiming the top spot on nearly every benchmark it touches. From billion-dollar balance sheets to benchmark battles to Arizona residents fighting data centers over water rights, today's roundup is a snapshot of an industry racing forward while the world scrambles to keep up.

stories.title: Google DeepMind unveils Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model with top benchmark scores
stories.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model emphasizing cybersecurity and long-horizon coding. It claims #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 at 59 and leads security benchmarks including SEC-bench Pro (88.2%), ExploitGym (54.8%), and CWE-bench (71.0%). It tops 15 of 17 benchmarks on Google's charts, with notable advantages in long-input reasoning, hacking, workflow automation, and math. Access is currently limited to select cyber defenders with no public release date. Rollout includes participation in U.S. government voluntary pre-release testing.
stories.opinion: Google is clearly positioning Carbon as its answer to Claude Opus 5.5, and the aggressive introductory pricing signals a willingness to compete on cost as well as capability. The cybersecurity focus is a savvy differentiator in a market where most frontier models compete on general benchmarks. However, restricting access to select defenders with no public timeline tempers the hype — until developers can actually use it, the benchmark claims are academic. Where coverage differs: DeepMind Blog says Carbon follows Gemini 4 Argon launched 'two weeks prior'; The Rundown AI says Argon was released 'just four weeks prior'. The Rundown AI reports introductory API pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens in/out that doubles after the promo period; DeepMind Blog does not mention pricing.

stories.title: Microsoft discloses Azure and OpenAI revenue for the first time, showing $33.2B and $10B respectively
stories.summary: Microsoft disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars for the first time, reporting $33.2 billion for the July-September 2026 quarter, up 48% year-over-year. Azure is now Microsoft's largest product line at about 36% of total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion. Separately, Microsoft reported $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI commercial arrangements in the same quarter, nearly 11% of total revenue. Full fiscal year 2026 OpenAI-related revenue totaled $24.1 billion. Microsoft also has $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI. The disclosures came alongside a corporate restructuring placing Azure in a new 'Agents and Infra' segment.
stories.opinion: These twin disclosures paint a picture of Microsoft as increasingly dependent on its AI bets paying off — Azure's dominance and the massive OpenAI revenue stream are now the company's defining financial story. The $7.2 billion in OpenAI receivables is worth watching; at some point the question of whether OpenAI can sustain these payments becomes material.

sources.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI
Microsoft just shared Azure’s actual revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion

cluster.reason: Both report on Microsoft's Q1 FY2027 earnings (quarter ending September 2026), covering Azure revenue and OpenAI-related revenue from the same quarterly results.

stories.title: Alphabet reports $127.6B quarterly revenue but Google Search ad growth decelerates, shares fall 8%
stories.summary: Alphabet reported $127.6 billion in Q3 2026 revenue, up 25% year-over-year, but Google Search ad revenue growth decelerated to 12% YoY from 17% in Q2 and 19% in Q1. Shares fell 8%. Google is expanding ads within AI-powered Search experiences to international markets for the first time. CEO Sundar Pichai said Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, with AI Mode queries averaging three times longer than traditional searches. Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30.7 billion. The Gemini app has reached 1 billion monthly users.
stories.opinion: The 8% share drop despite 25% revenue growth tells the story: investors are watching the Search ad growth deceleration as a proxy for whether AI cannibalizes Google's core cash machine. The international AI Search ads expansion looks like Google's attempt to prove it can monetize AI Mode before the slowdown becomes a rout.

stories.title: Arizona residents mobilize against data center water consumption as Colorado River allocation shrinks
stories.summary: A bipartisan grassroots coalition of Arizona residents is opposing new data center developments over water usage concerns. TSMC's chip factory near Phoenix consumes nearly 5 million gallons of water daily from the municipal supply, and Arizona now hosts 172 hyperscale data centers. The opposition is driven by Arizona's looming loss of nearly 30% of its Colorado River water allocation, making tech infrastructure water demands increasingly untenable. Residents have become self-taught experts on zoning, land use, and water consumption.
stories.opinion: This is the water version of the power-grid strain story that has defined AI infrastructure expansion. Arizona's situation is particularly acute because the Colorado River cuts are already locked in — this isn't hypothetical scarcity, it's arithmetic. The bipartisan nature of the opposition suggests this could become a genuine political constraint on data center siting in the American Southwest.

stories.title: Instagram's Mosseri says public negativity toward AI 'going to get worse' over next two years
stories.summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in a podcast interview that public negativity toward AI is growing and will worsen over the next couple of years, driven by anxiety, frustration, and anger — particularly in creative industries. He admitted Instagram probably doesn't rank AI content as well as non-AI content and acknowledged 'AI slop' is a real issue, though he thinks the term is used 'too liberally.' Instagram has been cracking down on AI-generated profiles and launching labels for AI accounts, though issues like celebrity deepfakes persist.
stories.opinion: Mosseri's candor is notable coming from a platform aggressively integrating AI features. His framing of concerns as 'fear of being left behind' rather than legitimate critiques of quality degradation may itself fuel the negativity he's predicting.

stories.title: Akai releases open-source MPC Sample Key, embracing vibe-coded mods built with AI
stories.summary: Akai is releasing the MPC Sample Key, a 37-key keyboard version of its budget MPC Sample, with open-source firmware. The company gave developers early access before the formal announcement, and the modding community has already built various synth mods — some using Claude. Akai's CEO confirmed plans to seed early devices to developers, open-source some software, and provide an SDK. The open-source approach may extend to the entire MPC Sample platform.
stories.opinion: A legacy hardware company open-sourcing firmware and actively courting AI-assisted modders is a fascinating inversion of the usual manufacturer-vs-modder dynamic. If the community delivers compelling synths and effects, Akai could get free R&D while selling more hardware — a smart play for a niche market.

stories.title: Human psychics push back against AI-generated readings, citing lack of empathy
stories.summary: Human psychics are pushing back against AI-generated readings, arguing that computer-generated divination lacks the empathy and personal connection that human practitioners provide. AI psychic chatbots like 'Urban Mystic' offer automated readings about auras, past lives, and predictions, while traditional practitioners warn these miss the interpersonal element central to their craft.
stories.opinion: This is a colorful entry in the broader 'AI displaces human practitioners' narrative. The irony of psychics arguing for the irreplaceable human element in an evidence-free practice aside, their core complaint — that AI lacks genuine empathy — echoes concerns from therapists, counselors, and other fields where the human relationship is arguably the product.

stories.title: MIT Tech Review report finds only 16% of organizations extract transformative value from AI
stories.summary: An MIT Technology Review Insights report, produced with Atlan, finds that while all surveyed organizations use AI, only 16% extract transformative value. The largest group (40%) sees only moderate gains. The report argues the missing piece is a 'context layer' — infrastructure between business systems and AI platforms that translates enterprise intelligence into governed, machine-usable context. Most companies remain in pilot phases (38%) or using AI as assistants (35%), with only 12% running AI agents in production and 3% using AI for most work in key processes.
stories.opinion: The finding that 100% of organizations use AI but only 16% get transformative value is the enterprise AI story in one stat. The 'context layer' framing is useful but unsurprising coming from a report sponsored by a metadata platform vendor. The real insight is the 3% figure for deep AI integration — the gap between AI adoption and AI transformation remains enormous.

stories.title: Documentary 'Hills and Mountains' recounts Afghan woman's story of forced marriage amid Soviet invasion
stories.summary: 'Hills and Mountains,' an 8-minute documentary directed by Afghan-born Canadian filmmaker Salar Pashtoonyar, tells the story of an Afghan woman born in 1969 whose life was transformed by the Soviet invasion in 1979. The film recounts how the invasion turned her homeland from 'peaceful and tolerant' to desperate, leading families to marry off teenage daughters to prevent starvation. Her own forced marriage followed a false accusation of an affair. The filmmaker uses landscapes of Afghanistan's mountains to connect geography, personal experience, and global history.
stories.opinion: A small, personal documentary that grounds sweeping geopolitical history in one woman's experience. The choice to use a voice actor and altered details to protect her identity underscores how dangerous these stories remain to tell, decades later.

stories.title: Pew finds divergent religiosity patterns among youngest U.S. adults versus slightly older peers
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center analysis finds mixed signals about religion among young U.S. adults. The very youngest adults (ages 18-22, born 2004-2008) report relatively high rates of religious service attendance. However, slightly older young adults (ages 23-26, born 2000-2003) are the least religious age group by measures of prayer frequency, importance of religion, religious identification, and monthly attendance.
stories.opinion: The divergence between 18-22 and 23-26 year-olds is intriguing — it could reflect a genuine generational shift, a life-stage effect where college-age adults temporarily re-engage, or simply noise in a narrow age band. Worth watching whether the younger cohort maintains its relative religiosity as it ages.

stories.title: Pew tracking study finds most Americans' individual religious lives held steady from 2020 to 2025
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center longitudinal study tracking 5,835 U.S. adults from 2020 to 2025 finds that most Americans' religious lives remained stable at the individual level. Religious affiliation, prayer frequency, and service attendance largely held steady. The study was designed to test whether stable national statistics mask offsetting individual changes, and concluded that for the majority, there was no significant shift in key religiousness indicators.
stories.opinion: This is methodologically significant: it confirms that national-level stability in religious metrics reflects genuine individual consistency rather than masking equal and opposite movements. The implication is that secularization in the U.S. is primarily a cohort-replacement story — each new generation is less religious, rather than existing adults drifting away.

here's how my remote dev setup evolved this year

it started with claude code on a linux pc in my room. tailscale + termius + tmux to reach it from my phone. it worked but usability was a pain and my wifi kept cutting out 

tried a vultr vps, not much better

realized it all sucked, quit my job, started a company

rebuilt on digitalocean. same termius + tmux pain, and couldn't use claude code remote control because i was account switching + using codex

then we moved all our boxes onto @useprized and built a web terminal that's actually good on a phone. no more ctrl+b 1 to switch tabs. then i switched to herdr and built that into it too

now it's rex by @superlogical on my prized boxes. i can hop between machines, see every session, and it's amazing on the duo

the terminal keeps changing, the boxes don't have to

tweet_headlines.author: noahkagan
tweet_headlines.headline: Noah Kagan found __17 of his 62 posts drove 64% of 1.5M views__ — and shares a Claude prompt to help you find your own top 3 formats.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
17 of my 62 posts got 64% of my 1.5M views.

Everyone says post more. I think 17 posts did the work, so find your 3 formats and repeat only those.

Mine:

1- "I looked at $46M of software sales on AppSumo."

The AppSumo Sales post: 98,585 views, 2,148 bookmarks. 5.4x my median.

2- A founder you know, real numbers, one lesson.

Sam Parr: 66,867 views. Laura Roeder: 71,748.

3- A prompt to copy.

The new-user onboarding prompt: 67,008 views, 1,462 bookmarks.

Find yours. Paste your last 60 posts with their views into Claude:

"Rank these posts by views. Find the 3 formats behind the top 10. For each one give the shared structure, the median views and the best example. Then tell me what the bottom 10 have in common."

Boring wins.

What are your 3 formats?
